item.title: U.S. Says It Struck 16 Iranian Mine-Laying Vessels Near Oil Route
item.summary: Whether any mines had been laid in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began on Feb. 28 is unclear. The Pentagon said 140 American service members had been wounded, eight severely, in the war.

item.title: Civilians Killed by Strikes in Gulf States Are Almost All Migrant Workers
item.summary: Since the American-Israeli attack on Iran began, at least 12 civilians have been killed in oil-rich Gulf countries. All but one of them were foreign nationals.

item.title: Fear and Hope for Iranians Trapped Between Bombs and Defiant Rulers
item.summary: Many in Iran feel helpless in the face of their entrenched system, and some are becoming increasingly embittered by the fierce American and Israeli bombardment.

item.title: Ukraine Helps U.S. Bases in the Mideast With Stopping Drones
item.summary: As the war in Iran spreads, Kyiv is eagerly offering its hard-won expertise and advanced technology to counter Iranian drones.

item.title: How Trump’s War With Iran Changed the World in a Week
item.summary: The conflict is reshaping travel patterns, energy dependencies, living costs, trade routes and diplomatic alliances.

item.title: World Heritage Sites Hit in Airstrikes on Iran
item.summary: Revered cultural icons that have withstood the upheavals of history are being hit hard in the war being waged by Israel and the United States.

item.title: Trump Casts a Shadow Over One of Mexico’s Deadliest States
item.summary: President Trump wants to strike cartels inside Mexico. In Sinaloa State, a cartel stronghold, some residents said they were willing to entertain U.S. intervention.

item.title: Mother of Tumbler Ridge Shooting Victim Sues OpenAI
item.summary: The company banned the shooter’s ChatGPT account but did not alert the authorities, a move that amounted to fatal negligence, the family claims.

item.title: On the Road With Zelensky, Weathered, Weary and Fighting On
item.summary: Ukraine’s leader, Volodymyr Zelensky, traveled east to visit frontline troops trying to stave off Russian attacks, and invited reporters for The New York Times to go with him.

item.title: China’s Military Has Quietly Cut Flying Near Taiwan. But Why?
item.summary: For years, China has flown military jets near Taiwan almost daily. Then they suddenly stopped, leaving analysts to wonder why.
